families.notes: Flat contiguous elementwise. All trident kernels target Triton ~2.1 (setup.py pins triton@main of 2023); several use APIs removed in Triton 3.x (tl.math.fast_expf/tanh/pow/max, tl.view) - porting needed for triton 3.6.
relu'(0)=0 as torch.
grad at x=0 is slope (same as torch).

Code implements the tanh approximation although trident.GELU docstring says plain GELU and tests compare to exact F.gelu(x) with atol=1e-2 (max diff ~5e-4). Intended reference ambiguous: 'tanh' (code) vs 'none' (nn.GELU default/tests). Uses tl.math.tanh (Triton 2.x API).
Same ambiguity as forward.
sigmoid via tl.math.fast_expf (approximate exp).

families.reference: F.gelu(x + b, approximate='tanh')  (x [M,N], b [N]); also stores shift = x + b
families.notes: Tests compare to exact F.gelu(x+b) at atol 1e-2; same tanh-vs-exact ambiguity as GELU.
Consumes saved shift; bias grad = grad_input.sum(0) in torch.
Input viewed [N, C, -1]; weight indexed per channel with bounds of C, so num_parameters=1 (module default) with C>1 reads out of bounds instead of broadcasting (torch broadcasts).

Kernel writes grad_input and a per-element weight-grad staging tensor g*min(x,0) shaped like input; wrapper sums only dim 2 -> grad_weight shape [N, C] instead of [C] for N>1 (wrapper bug, check staging tensor instead).

families.reference: torch.where(m, x/(1-p+2.22e-16), 0), m = tl.rand(seed, flat_offset) > p
families.notes: Deterministic check: conditional on mask (zeros of output where x!=0) kept values equal x/(1-p); fraction kept ~1-p. Seed = torch.random.seed(), which re-seeds torch's global RNG nondeterministically (side effect) and is a 64-bit value passed to a tl.int32-annotated arg.

families.reference: torch.where(m, g/(1-p), 0) with the forward mask m
families.notes: DEVIATION/BUG: mask inferred as (p==0)|(output>0) - kept elements with x<=0 get zero grad - and grad scaled by (1-p+eps) instead of 1/(1-p). Correct only for p in {0,1} (the only tested values).

Online max/sum per lane with tl.math.fast_expf. Edge deviation: when x_size % x_block_size != 0 and x_size > x_block_size, lanes padded in the last block rescale their partial sum by exp(max-0), overflowing (inf) for logits >~88 or underflowing (dropped mass) for logits <~-88.

families.reference: delta = (g*y).sum(dim); grad = y*(g - delta) == torch.autograd.grad(torch.softmax(x,dim), x, g)
families.notes: Takes saved output y. delta accumulated in input dtype (fp16 accumulation for fp16).
Mask convention fixed by code only: a mask value > eps EXCLUDES the position (true/1 = masked out); mask must share x's shape and strides. Fully masked row -> NaN. Whole row in one block (next_pow2).
No grad for mask.

families.reference: F.layer_norm(x, normalized_shape, weight, bias, eps)  (+ mean, rstd saved)
families.notes: Whole normalized extent in one block (next_pow2). mean/rstd stored in input dtype (fp16 precision for backward).

families.reference: torch.autograd.grad(F.layer_norm(x, ns, w, b, eps), (x, w), g)
families.notes: BUG (suspected): with padding (x_size not pow2) centered_mean is not masked, so padded lanes contribute 2*(-mean)*grad_var to grad_mean -> grad_input off by a per-row constant when mean != 0 (tests use randn rows, mean~0). dW via per-row staging summed in torch; bias grad computed in torch as grad_output.sum(0) (wrong shape for >2D inputs).

families.family: rms_norm forward (partial RMSNorm, eps outside sqrt)
families.reference: k = d if not 0<=p<=1 else int(d*p); rms = x[..., :k].pow(2).mean(-1, keepdim=True).sqrt(); x / (rms + eps) * w (+ b)
spec_sources: Zhang & Sennrich 2019 'Root Mean Square Layer Normalization' (pRMSNorm) and its reference code
families.notes: Not torch.nn.functional.rms_norm: eps is added to rms outside the sqrt. Kernel passes partial_size = d*p as a float constexpr: sums lanes with index < d*p (i.e. ceil) but divides by the float d*p, differing from the paper's int(d*p) when d*p is non-integer; p=0 divides by zero. Weight required; functional eps default 1e-8, module 1e-5. Saves rms.
Gradient through rms uses -x/(rms*rms + eps) instead of -x/(rms+eps)^2 (O(eps/rms) relative inconsistency with the forward). dW per-row staging summed in torch; bias grad in torch.
Input viewed [N, C, -1]; a whole group (C/G x L, each padded to pow2) in one block, so large groups may not compile. mean/rstd stored in input dtype.

families.reference: torch.autograd.grad(F.group_norm(x, G, w, b, eps), (x, w, b), g)
families.notes: grad_output/input loaded with boundary_check but no padding_option (undefined padding); dW/db staging sums include padded lanes along L, correct only if padding reads as 0. Staging [N, C] summed in torch.

families.reference: F.batch_norm(x, running_mean, running_var, weight, bias, training=True, momentum=momentum, eps=eps)  (x [N,C,L]; running stats updated in place with unbiased var if given)
families.notes: DEVIATION: function.batch_norm ignores its `training` argument and the module passes track_running_stats there; eval mode (normalize with running stats) is never used and running stats are updated even in eval. Whole [N, L] per channel in one block (next_pow2 each). mean/var saved in input dtype. momentum=None unsupported.

families.reference: torch.autograd.grad(F.batch_norm(x, None, None, w, b, training=True, eps=eps), (x, w, b), g)
F.instance_norm(x, running_mean, running_var, weight, bias, use_input_stats=use_input_stats, momentum=momentum, eps=eps)  (x [N,C,L])
families.notes: Running update = (1-m)*r + m*mean_over_batch(per-instance mean / unbiased var), same as torch. Module deviation: passes use_input_stats = not track_running_stats and ignores self.training, so with track_running_stats=True it always normalizes with running stats and never updates them. mean/var stored in input dtype; momentum is a constexpr.

families.reference: torch.autograd.grad(F.instance_norm(x, rm, rv, w, b, use_input_stats, m, eps), (x, w, b), g)
families.notes: DEVIATION: with use_input_stats=0 the kernel still applies the batch-statistics gradient formula (subtracting mean/var terms) although stats are constants; correct grad would be w*rsqrt(rv+eps)*g.
Accumulator dtype = input dtype: fp16 inputs accumulate in fp16 (tl.dot out_dtype=fp16); bf16 uses out_dtype fp16 then casts (range overflow >65504). use_accelerator=True enables TF32 for fp32.

families.family: linear backward (dX, per-batch dW, per-batch db)
families.reference: torch.autograd.grad(F.linear(x, W, b), (x, W, b), g)
families.notes: dW/db written per batch into staging [B, N, K]/[B, N] and summed in torch; low-precision accumulation as forward. Also used by GEGLU backward.

families.reference: h = F.linear(x, W, b); s, g = h.chunk(2, -1); s * F.gelu(g, approximate='tanh')  (also stores h)
families.notes: Conventions from code: first half = value, second half = gate, tanh GELU (paper uses exact GELU on the gate). BUG: boundary heuristics inverted (require_*_boundary_check = size % block == 0), so when K and M (or K and N/2) are not multiples of the block sizes loads run unchecked out of bounds. fp16 accumulation as Linear.

families.reference: torch.autograd.grad(geglu_ref(x, W, b), (x, W, b), g)
families.notes: GEGLU.backward produces grad of h from saved h (whole row of N/2 per program); then Linear backward kernels. ctx.use_accelerator forced False.

families.reference: F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=float_mask, is_causal=is_causal, scale=1/sqrt(D))  (q,k,v [B,H,N,D]); aux log2sum = rowwise max + log2(sum) of scaled scores in base-2
families.notes: Constraints: N and D powers of 2, D in {16,32,64,128}, q and k/v same N (y_size used for both), contiguous [B,H,N,D] (head offset = flat head index * stride(1)), float additive mask [B,H,N,N] (bool rejected), mask and is_causal mutually exclusive. No boundary checks: N must be a multiple of the autotuned block (16/32/64). Scores and output accumulate in input dtype (fp16 accumulation for fp16). log2sum stored in input dtype.

delta = rowsum(o*do) via Softmax.backward_delta; recomputes P from forward log2sum. dq accumulated read-modify-write into caller-zeroed buffer. Fixed block 64 with no boundary checks -> requires N >= 64 (pow2 N in {16,32} reads OOB). grad_mask = dS (grad w.r.t. additive mask).

families.reference: kernel: torch.where(m, sdpa_out/(1-p+eps), 0) with m = tl.rand(seed, arange(D) + y_block_offset) > p  (intended per signature: torch SDPA dropout on attention probabilities)
families.notes: DEVIATION: dropout applied to the normalized output, not to attention probabilities; mask indexed only by head-dim lane + row-block offset, so identical across rows of a block and across batch/heads, overlapping between blocks. Backward infers mask from output>0 and multiplies by (1-p+eps) instead of dividing. Deterministic check only conditional on the kernel's mask. Seed via torch.random.seed() (global RNG side effect).

families.reference: F.cosine_similarity(x1, x2, dim, eps)  [kernel formula: (x1*x2).sum(dim) / clamp(x1.norm(dim=dim)*x2.norm(dim=dim), min=eps)]
families.notes: Clamps the product of norms (older torch formula); current torch clamps each norm separately - differs only when a norm < eps. Inputs same shape, contiguous, rank<=3, no broadcasting. Also writes numerator/denominator for backward.

BUG: inside the loop over the reduced dim, ||x1|| and ||x2|| are recomputed from the current block only (tl.sum over block), so gradients are wrong whenever size_along_dim > autotuned block_size (256..2048). Divides by unclamped denominator (inf/NaN for zero vectors).
Ties -> first index (tl.argmax tie_break_left). NaN not propagated (torch treats NaN as max). Padding handled with -inf.

BUG: padded lanes (x_size not pow2) loaded with undefined padding and not masked; if padding reads 0 and all row values are negative, argmax lands on a padded index and the value is read out of row bounds. NaN handling differs from torch.
Scatters g to the saved argmax index; shapes are constexpr (recompile per shape).
Accumulates in input dtype (fp16 accumulation for fp16). function.sum(dim=None) reduces the last dim of a 2D tensor (torch: full reduction).
Accumulates in input dtype; dim=None behaves as last dim.
Per-lane Welford then tl.reduce with combine_welford (masked lanes use count += 2.2e-16). correction is constexpr; x_size == correction divides by zero (torch gives inf/nan similarly).
Recomputes the mean (input-dtype accumulation).
DEVIATION: only g_var is used; the wrapper discards the gradient of the mean output (missing + g_mean/N term).
